rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: The clause about punishment by God's will displays His power to punish or forgive, while He punishes only sinners.
rows.anchor: قادر على تعذيب من أشاء، وغفران من أشاء، ومبالغة في كونه قادرا، ولكن لا يعذب إلا العصاة، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed reading distinguishes punishment, which occurs by God's will, from forgiveness.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن وقوعه بمشيئة له دون المغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that God wills punishment only in cases of disobedience, with either description implying the other.
rows.anchor: والثالث: أنه لا يشاء ذلك إلا على معصية، فأيها ذكر دل على الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expansive mercy is God's blessing, which encompasses everything.
rows.anchor: قوله: (ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء) أي: نعمتي عمت كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says God can bestow blessing on anyone eligible to receive it.
rows.anchor: قيل: المراد أني أقدر أن أنعم على كل من يصح الإنعام عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the mercy here as applying specifically to believers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنها خاصة في المؤمنين، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Hasan and Qatada say God's blessings reach righteous and wicked people in this life, but belong to the righteous in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي نعم البر والفاجر في الدنيا، وفي الآخرة للبر خاصة عن الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the mercy as repentance that covers every sin.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي التوبة وسعت كل ذنب، عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I shall write it” means that God will make this mercy obligatory for those who are God-conscious.
rows.anchor: فسأكتبها أي: أوجبها يعني الرحمة للذين يتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies those who are God-conscious as people who avoid idolatry.
rows.anchor: قيل: يتقون الشرك، أي: يجتنبونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view identifies them as those who avoid major sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الكبائر، وقيل: جميع خصال التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view takes the phrase to include all qualities of piety.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جميع خصال التقوى ويؤتون الزكاة

rows.speaker: أبو علي وأبو مسلم وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: The zakat phrase means that they give the alms due on their wealth.
rows.anchor: قيل: يعطون زكاة أموالهم، عن أبي علي وأبي مسلم وأكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والأصم
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation makes giving zakat mean obeying God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يطيعون الله ورسوله، عن ابن عباس والحسن والأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing in God's signs means affirming His proofs; the three traits are paired because piety restrains sin, zakat is a demanding financial duty, and faith entails difficult knowledge of God, His Messenger, religion, and the resolution of doubts.
rows.anchor: بأدلتنا يؤمنون يصدقون، وإنما جمع بين هذه الآيات؛ لأن التقوى جامع من المنع عن المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports asking for the good things of this world just as one asks for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: تدل الآية على حسن سؤال نعيم الدنيا كما يحسن سؤال الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A supplicant should approach God through repentance and sincerity, as in “we have turned to You.”
rows.anchor: الواجب على الداعي أن يتقرب بدعاء التوبة والإخلاص؛ لذلك قالوا: إنا هدنا إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants blessings to both righteous and wicked people but reserves afterlife reward for believers; this answers Moses' request for worldly and religious good after the earthquake.
rows.anchor: أنه - تعالى - ينعم على البر والفاجر، ويخص بالثواب المؤمن؛ فلذلك فصل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the descendants word as a plural, with an alif and kasra on the tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: من ظهورهم ذرياتهم بالألف وكسر التاء على الجمع

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use the singular form, without an alif and with fatḥa on the tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي: ذريتهم بغير ألف وفتح التاء على الواحد

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr reads “that they say” with yāʾ as a report about them; the other readers use tāʾ for direct address in both instances.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: شهدنا أن يقولوا بالياء على الخبر عنهم، وقرأ الباقون بالتاء فيهما على الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhurriyya is a collective whose plural is dhurriyyāt; it is also analyzed on the pattern faʿīliyya, like qamariyya, and linked to dharr because of smallness.
rows.anchor: الذرية جمعها ذريات، وذرية قيل فعلية نحو قمرية، وأصله من الذر، شبه به لصغرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed etymology connects the descendants to their emergence from the loins like tiny ants.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنهم يخرجون من الأصلاب كالذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further etymology derives the word from God's creating the creatures, using dharaʾa.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من ذرأ الله الخلق أي: خلقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafṣīl is to distinguish truth from falsehood; faṣala means to decide or clarify between disputants, and al-fayṣal is a judge.
rows.anchor: والتفصيل: تبيين الحق من الباطل، فصلت الأمر فصلا، والفيصل: الحاكم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The governing verb for “when” is omitted and understood as “remember.”
rows.anchor: العامل في قوله: وإذ قيل محذوف، وتقديره: واذكر، عن أبي علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “their descendants” is genitive as the object of “took,” whereas the singular form is accusative.
rows.anchor: وكسرنا ذرياتهم؛ لأنه مفعول (أخذ)، فيكسر في الجمع، وينصب في الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Or that you say” is accusative, coordinated with the earlier “that you say” and governed by أن.
rows.anchor: أو تقولوا محله نصب عطفا على تقولوا فنصبه ب (أن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in “likewise” is comparative, and “that” signals clarification following clarification.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الكاف كاف التشبيه، و(ذلك) يقتضي بيانا بعد بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account links the verse to the monotheistic proofs before the prophetic narratives, including God's creation and sending the winds, then sees it as a return to proofs of oneness and condemnation of idolatry.
rows.anchor: تتصل بدلائل التوحيد المذكورة قبل قصص الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account connects this covenant with the preceding covenant requiring the Children of Israel to act by the Torah, then extends the covenant to all Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: يتصل بما قبله من أخذ الميثاق على بني إسرائيل بأن يعملوا بالتوراة، ثم عقبه بأخذ الميثاق على جميع بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among several proposed constructions, the closest takes God to remind the descendants that their extraction from their fathers' loins had already been shown to them, so they cannot claim ignorance or merely imitate their fathers.
rows.anchor: أقربها أن تقديرها: وإذا أخذ ربكم من ظهور بني آدم ذريتهم، وأشهدهم على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: أبو علي وقاضي القضاة
rows.claim: Abu Ali's and the Chief Judge's chosen view understands the testimony as occurring through God's prophets: if people were thus charged, they would obey and could not plead ignorance or parental imitation; those with an excuse are mercifully not punished, and the account concerns only a particular group.
rows.anchor: فلا بد أن يكون خاصا في قوم، وهذا قول شيخنا أبي علي، واختيار قاضي القضاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two preceding interpretations of the covenant are both valid.
rows.anchor: وكل واحد من هذين الوجهين يصح

rows.speaker: أصحاب الحديث
rows.claim: Hadith transmitters report that God extracted Adam's descendants in two groups, assigning one to Paradise and one to Hell; in a prophetic report, a man asks what deeds are for, while Umar's version asks why people were sent, and the Prophet answers that each is facilitated for what he was created for.
rows.anchor: يرويه أصحاب الحديث عن أسلافهم من الآثار موقوفة ومرفوعة ويجعلون ذلك تأويلا للآية

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report attributed to Abu Hurayra says every soul to be created until Resurrection fell from Adam's back; Adam was shown his descendants, saw David's light, gave him forty years of his own lifespan, then denied the recorded gift and his descendants denied it.
rows.anchor: ورووا في حديث أبي هريرة: أنه مسح ظهره فسقط من ظهره كل نسمة هو خالقها إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the descendants were made like ants and answered the divine question affirmatively and obediently.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أخذ مثل الذر فقال: ألست بربكم؟ قالوا: بلى طائعين طائعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report predicts that the Hour will not come until everyone whose covenant was taken has been born.
rows.anchor: ورووا أنه لا تقوم الساعة حتى يولد كل من أخذ ميثاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report has God extract white descendants from Adam's right side for Paradise by mercy and black descendants from his left for Hell, identifying them with the people of the right and left.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار: أنه أخرج من صفحة ظهره اليمنى ذرية بيضاء، وقال لهم: ادخلوا الجنة برحمتي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported location for the covenant is ʿArafa.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في أي موضع كان، قيل: بعرفة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported location for the covenant is India.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بالهند

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported location for the covenant is heaven.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في السماء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported location for the covenant is between Mecca and Taif.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بين مكة والطائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author quotes an admonition warning Balaam against cursing Gods Prophet and the believers.
rows.anchor: وقال: ويحك يا بلعم، أتدعو على نبي الله والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Balaam report is authentic, the donkey's rebuke is a miracle for Moses, since a miracle cannot be manifested for liars.
rows.anchor: وهذا إن صح فهو معجزة لموسى (عليه السلام)؛ لأنه لا يجوز إظهار المعجزة على الكذابين

rows.speaker: حمزة والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: These readers use the open-yāʾ and open-ḥāʾ form yalḥadūna here and in the cited passages; al-Kisāʾī agrees in al-Naḥl.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب يلحدون بفتح الياء والحاء هاهنا، وفي (النحل)

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī also reads the open form in al-Naḥl.
rows.anchor: ووافقه الكسائي في (النحل)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use the closed-yāʾ, kasra-ḥāʾ form; both forms are valid Arabic and mean deviation from the truth.
rows.anchor: والباقون جميع ذلك بضم الياء وكسر الحاء وهما لغتان صحيحتان

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī distinguishes ilḥād from luḥūd and takes the al-Naḥl usage to mean inclination or reliance.
rows.anchor: فأما الكسائي فكان يفرق بين الإلحاد واللحود، ويقول: التي في (النحل) بمعنى الركون

rows.speaker: الأحمر
rows.claim: Al-Aḥmar says laḥadt means to deviate, while alḥadt means to argue or dispute, citing the phrase about a foreign tongue.
rows.anchor: وقال الأحمر: لحدت: جرت وملت، وألحدت: جادلت وماريت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dharaʾa, inshāʾ, iḥdāth, and khalq are synonyms meaning creation.
rows.anchor: الذرأ والإنشأء والإحداث والخلق نظائر، ويقال: ذرأ الله الخلق أي: خلقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An “ism” signifies a meaning without being bound to time; some names describe an attribute such as power or knowledge, while others are pure titles, and ḥusnā is the feminine of ḥasan.
rows.anchor: والاسم ما دل على معنى غير مقرون بزمان، ثم ينقسم، فمنه ما يفيد صفة في المسمى كقولنا: قادر عالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥād is departing from the intended course, originally meaning to incline; laḥd is the side niche in a grave, and the related grave terms name the same feature.
rows.anchor: والإلحاد: العدول عن القصد، وأصله الميل، ومنه: لحد القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Justice is fairness: one should practice what one urges, rather than command virtue while neglecting oneself.
rows.anchor: والعدل: النصف، ومن النصفة أن تعمل ما تدعو إليه، لا أن تكون كمن يأمر بالبر وينسى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “for Hell” marks an outcome, not an original purpose: they were made for reward and mercy, but disobedience led them to Hell, making the outcome seem like their purpose.
rows.anchor: اللام في قوله: لجهنم لام العاقبة، وتقديره: ذرأنا كثيرا من الجن والإنس للثواب والرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outcome-use of lām is established in Arabic by al-Akhfash, Qutrub, al-Zajjāj, al-Mubarrad, and other linguists, who cite Arab usage.
rows.anchor: ذكرها جماعة من أهل اللغة كالأخفش وقطرب والزجاج والمبرد، وحكوا ذلك عن العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic example of Pharaoh's household taking Moses as a child shows an outcome contrary to their stated intention to find comfort in him.
rows.anchor: (فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا) وإنما التقطوه قالوا: قرة عين لي ولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poetic line uses the lām of consequence for gathering wealth that heirs will inherit and building houses that time will ruin.
rows.anchor: أموالنا لذوي الميراث نجمعها ... ودورنا لخراب الدهر نبنيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second anonymous poetic line uses the same consequence construction: mothers nourish their young for death, as houses are built for ruin.
rows.anchor: وللموت تغذو الوالدات سخالها ... كما لخراب الدور تبني المساكن

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali cites an unnamed pre-Islamic poet's line about a mother giving birth to a child who will die as evidence for consequence lām.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أبو علي لشاعر جاهلي: أأم سماك فلا تجزعي ... فللموت ما تلد الوالده

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim cites a poem saying every mother gives birth to a child destined for death as evidence for consequence lām.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أبو مسلم: يا أم وجرة بعض الوجد واعترفي ... فكل والدة للموت ما تلد

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa cites the saying “give birth for death and build for ruin” as evidence, and calls the lām an iḍāfa lām used both for cause and something resembling cause.
rows.anchor: وأنشد علي بن عيسى: لدوا للموت وابنوا للخراب ... فكلكم يصير إلى التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daʾb means habit, way, or customary practice; the passage gives its verbal forms and illustrates its use in a line about tribes breaking apart.
rows.anchor: الدأب. والعادة والطريقة والسنة سواء، دأب يدأب دأبا ودؤوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses daʾb for customary conduct in a line describing the collapse of Hawazin, Sulaym, and Amir.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: وما زال ذاك الدأب حتى تخاذلت ... هوازن وارفضت سليم وعامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says daʾb originally derives from the verb meaning to persist in doing something, but Arabs shifted it to mean a matter or way.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: الدأب أصله من دأبت، إلا أن العرب حولت معناه إلى الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika points to something absent; its original form is dhāka, with an added lām marking distance.
rows.anchor: و(ذلك): إشارة إلى غائب، والأصل ذاك، زيدت اللام علامة لبعد المشار إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing something makes it unlike its former state; taghayyara describes the occurrence of something different within it.
rows.anchor: والتغيير يصير الشيء خلاف ما كان عليه، غيره تغييرا، وتغير تغيرا، وهو أن يحصل فيه غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “like the way of Pharaoh's people” is a predicate of an implied subject, estimated as “their way is like the way of Pharaoh's people,” and is nominative.
rows.anchor: العامل في قوله: كدأب آل فرعون الابتداء، تقدير: دأبهم كدأب آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn is omitted from yakun because of frequent use, without loss of meaning.
rows.anchor: ولم يك حذفت النون لكثرة الاستعمال من غير إخلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says the verse was revealed about Meccans who drove the Prophet toward the Khazraj and were then killed at Badr.
rows.anchor: قيل: نزلت في أهل مكة لما أخرجوا النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إلى الخزرج ثم قتلوا يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse compares the state of these disbelievers to that of Pharaoh's people; the comparison may instead point back to the preceding mention of the way of earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: ثم بين - تعالى - أن حال هؤلاء الكفار كحال من قبلهم، فقال: كدأب الكاف كاف التشبيه

rows.speaker: الأخفش وأبو عبيدة والمؤرج والأصم وأبو علي وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: These authorities interpret the comparison as the customary conduct of Pharaoh's people and their followers.
rows.anchor: كعادة آل فرعون أي: قومه وأتباعه، عن الأخفش وأبي عبيدة والمؤرج والأصم وأبي علي وأبي مسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak interpret the comparison as Pharaoh's people's action and character.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كفعلهم وصفتهم، عن ابن عباس والضحاك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes the phrase to mean the affair or condition of Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كشأن آل فرعون وأمرهم، عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī understands the comparison to mean that Pharaoh's people disbelieved just as the addressees did.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان آل فرعون كفروا كما كفرتم، عن الكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage establishes acting on a single transmitter's report, since otherwise ordering people to convey it would have no purpose.
rows.anchor: تدل على وجوب العمل بخبر الواحد؛ لأنه لو لم يلزم العمل بتعريفهم لم يكن للأمر به معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious knowledge may be taken from someone who is not infallible, contrary to the Imami position.
rows.anchor: يجوز أخذ الدين والعلم ممن ليس بمعصوم، فيبطل قول الإمامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jihad is obligatory and should begin with the nearest enemy when circumstances are equal; a farther enemy may take priority if feared while the nearer one is safe, and combining both campaigns is preferable when possible.
rows.anchor: وجوب الجهاد وكيفيته، وأن الواجب البداية بالأقرب فالأقرب، وهذا عند تساوي الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith increases and decreases because God explicitly mentions its increase, which implies that deeds are part of faith.
rows.anchor: الإيمان يزيد وينقص؛ لأنه تعالى نص على زيادة الإيمان وذلك يوجب أن يكون العمل من الإيمان

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعلي بن أبي طالب والحسن ومجاهد وابن المبارك
rows.claim: The view that faith increases and decreases is attributed to Umar, Ali, Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn al-Mubarak, and other Companions.
rows.anchor: قول عمر بن الخطاب، وعلي بن أبي طالب، والحسن، ومجاهد، وابن المبارك، وغيرهم من الصحابة

rows.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: These readers use the taʾ-address form “do you not see,” addressing the believers; the other readers use yāʾ to report about the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة ويعقوب: أولا ترون بالتاء على الخطاب للمؤمنين، وهو قراءة أبي بن كعب، وقرأ الباقون بالياء خبرا عن المنافقين

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads the phrase as “Have they not seen?” with an added negative particle.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش أولم يروا

rows.speaker: طلحة وعبد الله
rows.claim: Talha reads the singular “does he not see?”; the source identifies this as Abdullah's reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة: أولا يرى، وهي قراءة عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading of anfusikum with ḍamma means the Messenger is from your lineage.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: أنفسكم بضم الفاء من النفس أي: من نسبكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والزهري وابن علية
rows.claim: These readers use fatḥa and understand the Messenger to be among the most noble and excellent of you, from the word nafīs, something prized.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والزهري وابن علية: من أنفسكم بفتح الفاء؛ أي: من أشرفكم وأفضلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common kasra reading makes “the Great” an adjective of the Throne.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة: العظيم بكسر الميم على أنه نعت للعرش

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads the ending in the nominative, making “the Great” an adjective of the Lord's name.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن محيصن بالرفع على أنه نعت لاسم الرب

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm prefers the nominative, estimated as “and He is the Great,” but the author rejects this preference as contrary to transmitted readings.
rows.anchor: قال الأصم: والرفع أعجب إلي، بتقدير: وهو العظيم، وليس بشيء؛ لأنه خلاف القراء والنقل

rows.speaker: بلال بن أبي بردة وابن محيصن
rows.claim: The common recitation has a light an followed by nominative al-ḥamd; Bilal ibn Abi Burda and Ibn Muḥayṣin double anna and put al-ḥamd in the accusative as its noun, with “to God, Lord of the worlds” as its predicate.
rows.anchor: قرأ بلال بن أبي بردة وابن محيصن بتشديد (أن)، الحمد نصب على أنه اسم (أن)، وخبرها في قوله: لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Liqāʾ is the verbal noun of meeting and can mean seeing; describing the meeting of what only God can bring about as meeting God magnifies its importance.
rows.anchor: جعل ملاقاة ما لا يقدر عليه إلا الله تعالى لقاء له تفخيما لشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghafla and sahw are near synonyms, opposed to wakefulness, and describe meaning departing from the self.
rows.anchor: والغفلة والسهو من النظائر، ونقيضه: اليقظة، وهو ذهاب المعنى عن النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥiyya is an honoring through a noble condition; a king is called a taḥiyya because he is greeted, and the word comes from wishing someone a good life.
rows.anchor: والتحية، التكرمة بالحال الجلية، ويسمون الملك تحية، لأن الملك يحيا بالتحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poetic line uses taḥiyya for a prize or honor a young man may attain.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: ولكل ما نال الفتى ... قد نلته إلا التحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daʿwā is derived from supplication, as shakwā is from complaint; supplication means asking someone to do something.
rows.anchor: الدعوى من الدعاء، كالشكوى من الشكاء، والدعاء: السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the syntax, the kāf of ulāʾika is an address particle, ulāʾika refers to the distant, and hāʾulāʾi to those present; the latter form is built on kasra at a meeting of two vowelless letters.
rows.anchor: الكاف في قوله: أولئك حرف الخطاب، وليس باسم، و(أولئك) لما بعد، و (هؤلاء) لمن حضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mīm of Allāhumma functions like yāʾ, so the expression is equivalent to “O God”; daʿwāhum is analyzed as a subject with a verb implied.
rows.anchor: والميم في (اللهم) معناه معنى (يا)، كأنه يقول: يا الله، وهو ياء النداء دعواهم يدعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥiyyatuhum is the subject and salām its predicate.
rows.anchor: تحيتهم اسم مبتدأ، وسلام خبر الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥānaka is not nominative like salām because its construction is understood as “I glorify You with glorification.”
rows.anchor: ولم يرفع سبحانك كما رفعت سلام؛ لأن سبحانك تقديره: سبحت سبحانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥamd is nominative because what follows the weakened an as its predicate is nominative.
rows.anchor: الحمد رفع؛ لأن ما يخبر بعد (أن) المخففة يكون رفعا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says a servant should not ask God for something He has said He will not do; this supports the view that God does no wrong, since one could otherwise ask Him not to do it and would owe Him no approval, but disapproval and hatred.
rows.anchor: أبو علي: وذلك يدل على أنه لا يحسن من العبد أن يسأله ما يعلم أنه تعالى لا يفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Building the ark counts as a religious duty because it is difficult work that God commanded.
rows.anchor: عمل السفينة داخل في التكليف؛ لأنه عمل شاق، مأمور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mocking people of religion is a grave sin, and the mockery is their own act rather than something created by God.
rows.anchor: أن تلك السخرية فعلهم، ليست بخلق لله تعالى

rows.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: Hafs reads kull with tanwīn, meaning a pair from every kind, and ithnayn then emphasizes the dual; the same reading occurs in al-Muʾminūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم: من كل زوجين اثنين بتنوين (كل)، أي: من كل صنف زوجين، وذكر (اثنين) تأكيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use the genitive construct without tanwīn and understand each pair as male and female.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون غير منون على الإضافة في السورتين يعني: زوجين: ذكر وأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fawr means boiling and originally rising; it also describes a pot boiling, anger surging, or acting before something settles.
rows.anchor: الفور: الغليان، وأصله الارتفاع، فارت القدر تفور، وفار غضبه: إذا جاش

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says a pair can be any two complementary things, such as heaven and earth, winter and summer, or night and day; God alone is one and unlike anything.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن في قوله: (ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين) السماء زوج، والأرض زوج، والشتاء زوج، والصيف زوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pair can mean male and female; for plants, zawj can mean a color, as in the phrase “a lovely pair.”
rows.anchor: ويقال: زوجان للذكر والأنثى، والزوج من النبات اللون، ومنه: (زوج بهيج)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage describes the drowning of Noah's people and the salvation of those aboard, beginning with the ship; “our command came” can mean the punishment or the command to destroy his people.
rows.anchor: ثم بين حال غرقهم ونجاة من في السفينة، وابتدأ بذكر أول أحوال السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “the tannūr boiled” may mean that the punishment arrived; alternatively, water sprang from Noah's bread oven as a sign.
rows.anchor: قيل: معناه فلما جاء أمرنا قيل: عذابنا، وقيل: أمرنا بهلاك قومه وفار التنور نبع الماء منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وأبو علي
rows.claim: These authorities identify the tannūr as Noah's bread oven, from an unusual place where water emerged as a sign for him.
rows.anchor: قيل: نبع الماء من موضع لا يعهد خروجه منه علامة لنوح، وهو تنور الخبز، عن ابن عباس، والحسن، ومجاهد، وأبي علي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة وأبو عيينة والزهري
rows.claim: These authorities say the water burst from the earth's surface, which Arabs call a tannūr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: انفجر الماء من وجه الأرض، والعرب تسمي وجه الأرض تنورا، عن ابن عباس، وعكرمة، وأبي عيينة، والزهري

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali interprets the boiling tannūr as the dawn breaking and the morning light appearing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فار التنور طلع الفجر نور الصبح، عن علي - عليه السلام -

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the tannūr is the most elevated and honored place on earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: التنور أشرف موضع في الأرض، وأعلى مكانا، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim reads the phrase figuratively as the crisis intensifying and water increasing, signaling Noah to save himself and his companions in the ship.
rows.anchor: ومعناه: إذا رأيت الأمر يشتد، والماء يكثر، فانج بنفسك ومن معك إلى السفينة، عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushd is the opposite of error, and rashīd describes one who guides toward good; rushd and rashad are two pronunciations.
rows.anchor: الرشد: نقيض الغي، والرشيد: الهادي إلى الخير، والرشد بضم الراء وسكون الشين والرشد بفتحها لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms qadima, qaddama, aqdama, and istaqdama all express advancing or going ahead; the last is illustrated by the cited verse.
rows.anchor: ويقال: قدم يقدم، مثل نصر ينصر. قدما، وقدم يقدم، مثل علم يعلم: إذا تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wurūd means entering; ward may mean departure's opposite, a water source, a turn at the water, or camels arriving there, and mawrūd is its passive participle.
rows.anchor: والورود: الدخول، والورد: خلاف الصدر، والورد: الماء الذي يورد عليه، والورد أيضا يوم النوبة

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari explains the criminals' arrival as walking thirsty like camels coming to water.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري: مشاة عطاشا كالإبل ترد الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafd originally means aid; a gift is called rafd because it helps its recipient, and the word also describes assistance, receiving a gift, cooperation, and Quraysh's pooled fund for pilgrims' food.
rows.anchor: والرفد أصله: العون على الأمر، فسمى العطية رفدا؛ لأنها عون للمعطى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿna is accusative as the predicate of a passive construction, while the unexpressed subject of “they were followed” is estimated to be Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: لعنة نصب؛ لأنه خبر ما لم يسم فاعله، والاسم الضمير في قوله: وأتبعوا تقديره: أتبع قوم فرعون اللعنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sent with God's proofs; one view identifies them as the staff and hand, while another includes all the evidences.
rows.anchor: بآياتنا أي: حججنا، قيل: العصا واليد، عن الأصم، وقيل: سائر الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm identifies the signs as the staff and hand.
rows.anchor: قيل: العصا واليد، عن الأصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A clear sultan is a manifest proof capable of defeating every false doctrine; the paired terms may simply differ in wording, or distinguish a great sign from the force to refute falsehood.
rows.anchor: وسلطان مبين أي: حجة بينة واضحة سلطت على إبطال كل مذهب فاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says the verses and sultan differ: the former is a great sign and the latter a force for refuting falsehood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناهم مختلف، فالأول من جهة أنها عبرة عظيمة، والثاني: من جهة أنه قوة على إبطال أمر المبطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's malāʾ means either his group or the leading people among his nation.
rows.anchor: إلى فرعون وملئه قيل: جماعته، وقيل: أشراف قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people followed Pharaoh's error by imitation and abandoned Moses' guidance despite the proofs, as common people tend to do.
rows.anchor: فاتبعوا أمر فرعون أي: اتبعوا ضلالة فرعون تقليدا، وتركوا هدى موسى مع الحجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Pharaoh's command was not guided” means it neither commanded right conduct nor guided to good; alternatively, it refers to his denial of Moses or his claim to be the highest lord.
rows.anchor: وما أمر فرعون برشيد أي: لا يأمر برشد، ولا يهدي إلى خير، وقيل: في تكذيب موسى

rows.speaker: نادغ وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: These readers use the passive “the matter is returned,” with al-amr as its nominative subject.
rows.anchor: قرأ نادغ، وحفص عن عاصم: وإليه يرجع الأمر بضم الياء وفتح الجيم على ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use the active form, attributing the return to the matter itself.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح الياء وكسر الجيم على أن الفعل مضاف إلى الأمر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم ويعقوب
rows.claim: These readers address the audience with “what you do”; the remaining readers use a third-person report, with the same disagreement in al-Naml.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر، ونافع، وابن عامر، وحفص عن عاصم، ويعقوب: وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣaṣ is a report of events following one another; qassahu means to follow its trace, as in the instruction to Moses' sister to follow him, or the narrative may trace the subject's path.
rows.anchor: القصص: الخبر عن الأمور التي يتلو بعضها بعضا، قصه: إذا اتبع أثره، ومنه: (وقالت لأخته قصيه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabaʾ is news about something momentous, as in the description of the Qur'an as a great report.
rows.anchor: والنبأ: الخبر عما فيه عظمة الشأن، من قولهم لهذا الخبر نبأ، ومنه: (قل هو نبأ عظيم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tathbīt means making something firm; it can establish, steady, report its existence, or prove that it exists.
rows.anchor: والتثبيت: تمكين إقامة الشيء، ثبته تثبيتا: إذا مكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makāna is a course on which one can act or a person's standing; Ibn ʿArfa defines enabling as removing impediments.
rows.anchor: والمكانة: الطريقة التي يتمكن من العمل عليها، يقال: له مكانة عند فلان، أي: قدر وجاه

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArfa defines enabling as the removal of obstacles.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عرفة: التمكين: زوال الموانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waiting means seeking to apprehend what is expected to come, and derives from looking.
rows.anchor: والانتظار: طلب الإدراك بما يأتي من الأمر، وأصله من النظر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses kullan as a verbal noun with the estimate “all the stories We recount to you,” and takes “what strengthens your heart” as an apposition.
rows.anchor: نصب (كلا) على المصدر، بتقدير: كل القصص نقص عليك، ويكون ما نثبت به فؤادك بدلا عنه، عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim instead parses kull as the object: “We recount to you all that strengthens your heart,” making kullan an adverbial accusative.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: هو مفعول به، يريد كلا نقص عليك ما نثبت به فؤادك، فيكون (كلا) منصوبا على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “what strengthens your heart,” mā is accusative as the object of the verb recount, and fuʾādaka is accusative as the object of making firm.
rows.anchor: و (ما) في قوله: (نثبت به فؤادك) منصوب بوقوع الفعل عليه، والعامل فيهما واحد، وهو قوله: نقص
